predecessors.name: Kingdom of Macedon
predecessors.text: Antigonus's share of Alexander's empire, 'Greece, Asia Minor, Syria, Phoenicia and northern Mesopotamia', made a kingdom when 'Antigonus assumed the title of king' in 306

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Macedon
predecessors.text: Macedon, Thessaly and the Antipatrid garrisons in Greece, taken by Demetrius Poliorcetes in 294

successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: Macedon, 'divided into four merides' (Amphipolis, Thessalonica, Pella, Pelagonia) in 167 as Roman client republics, a province from 146

ledger.x: 306: Antigonus takes the title of king.
304-303: Demetrius 'returned a second time to Greece as liberator, and reinstated the Corinthian League'; 'In 304-303 he seized cities including Corinth'.
301: Ipsus. 'Antigonus died during the battle in his eighty-first year after being struck by a javelin'; 'The empire was carved up between the victors'.
301: western Asia Minor to Lysimachus ('Lysimachus receiving the remainder of Asia Minor', Ipsus page).
301: Syria and the east of Anatolia to Seleucus ('Seleucus expanding his power to eastern Asia Minor'; Syria is the Diadochi page's reading).

288: Pyrrhus and Lysimachus 'decided to share rulership over Macedonia'; Pyrrhus kept his share until 'In 284 BC, he was driven out of Macedon by Lysimachus' (285 on the Lysimachus page). kingdom-of-epirus gains Western Macedonia only.
288 (bridged): Thessaly leaves Demetrius with his Macedon.
c. 287: Athens revolts. 'Meanwhile, Athens revolted' (undated on the page; the revolt is usually placed in 287); Piraeus stayed Macedonian on the usual account, which the page does not say.
277/276: the court returns to Pella ('Pella (since Antigonus II)').

c. 275: Aegium expels the Macedonian garrison. 'Around the year 275 BC, the people expelled the Macedonian garrison and the city joined the new Achaean League' (Aigio page). Mirrors achaean-league's 275 gain; 'around' keeps the confidence at 2.
272: Pyrrhus killed at Argos; 'his whole army and camp surrendered to Antigonus, greatly increasing his power'.
261-229: Athens as a Macedonian dependency (rule 4 tint).

c. 253: Alexander of Corinth revolts, 'the most serious threat to the Macedonian hegemony in Greece'. The page gives no start year (usually c. 253/252); Antigonus 'regained control of Corinth in the winter of 245/44 BC'.
229: Argos goes over to the Achaeans ('Argos in 229 BC', Achaean League page).
223: 'Antigonus proceeded to capture Mantinea, Heraea, and Telphusa, which confined Cleomenes to Laconia'; Heraea and Orchomenus 'went to Macedon' (infobox), Mantinea to the Achaeans.
219: Philip's campaigns in the Social War.
217: Phthiotic Thebes taken ('Philip took the city of Thebes in Phthiotic Achaea'); the peace of Naupactus (217) let 'every side... maintain what it currently possessed'.
217: the Peace of Naupactus ends the Social War; infobox 'Macedonian and Achaean victory'.
217: Philip V takes Bylazora from the Dardani.
214: the First Macedonian War opens in Illyria.
211: Laevinus hands Oeniadae and Nasos to the Aetolians.
205: Phoenice ends the First Macedonian War ('stalemate and Peace of Phoenice').
200: the Second Macedonian War (infobox 'March 200 - June 197 BC').
196: the fetters pass to Roman garrisons until 'the legions were not completely evacuated until 194 BC'; Corinth had 'earlier [been] promised... to the Achaeans'.
196: Orestis freed and the Asian and Thracian garrisons withdrawn ('Philip had to remove all his garrisons in Greek cities in Europe and Asia, which were to be free and autonomous').
196: the Boeotians, Philip's allies at Phoenice (205), leave the Macedonian orbit with the proclamation of 'the Freedom of the Greeks'.
191: Macedon takes Demetrias from the Aetolians.

c. 185: the Thessalian towns of 191 surrendered. No page opened dates this (the Roman commission of 185/184 on the usual account); Cliopatria's 170 shape (43,431 km2) has lost them. Demetrias and the Magnesian coast stayed Macedonian on the usual account; the page is silent.
c. 185: the Athamanian lands of 191 surrendered (undated on the pages opened; same bridge as the Thessalian towns).
168: the Molossian alliance ends with Pydna; in 167 Roman troops 'were sent to seventy cities' of Epirus and '150,000 people were enslaved'.
168: the Antigonid kingdom ends at Pydna; 'the Antigonid kingdom was dissolved and replaced by four republics' (Perseus page).

wars.name: Fourth War of the Diadochi (Ipsus)
wars.outcome: 'Antigonid defeat' (Diadochi infobox): Antigonus killed at Ipsus (301); his kingdom 'carved up between the victors', Lysimachus taking western Asia Minor, Seleucus the east and Syria; Demetrius kept his fleet, Cyprus and Greek cities.

wars.name: Demetrius's wars in Greece and Macedon
wars.outcome: Athens and the Macedonian throne taken in 294; Boeotia resecured in 291; in 288 Pyrrhus, Ptolemy and Lysimachus 'obliged him to leave Macedonia' and divided it.

wars.name: Gallic invasion and the Battle of Lysimachia
wars.outcome: 'In 277 BC, Antigonus II Gonatas defeated the Gauls at the Battle of Lysimachia' and 'claim[ed] the Macedonian throne'; the survivors founded Tyle in Thrace and others crossed to Asia as the Galatians.

wars.name: Pyrrhus's invasion of Macedon
wars.outcome: Pyrrhus 'seized the Macedonian throne from Antigonus II Gonatas in 274 BC and invaded the Peloponnese in 272 BC'; killed 'during a street battle at Argos' in 272, after which his army surrendered to Antigonus.

wars.name: Chremonidean War
wars.outcome: 'Macedonian victory' that 'confirmed Antigonid control over Greece': Athens garrisoned; the Ptolemaic fleet 'defeated off Cos (probably in 261 BC)'.

wars.name: Revolt of Alexander of Corinth
wars.outcome: Corinth recovered 'in the winter of 245/44 BC'; the start year is not on the page.

wars.name: Demetrian War
wars.outcome: 'It was only during the reign of Demetrios II (239-229) that Aitolia and Macedonia were at war' (Aetolian League page); Boeotia submitted (236); Agron's Illyrians relieved Medion (232/231); 'the Dardani defeated Demetrius who died shortly the next spring'…

wars.name: Cleomenean War (Macedonian intervention)
wars.outcome: 'Achaean and Macedonian victory'; 'Acrocorinth, Corinth, Heraea, and Orchomenus went to Macedon'; Antigonus entered Sparta but did not force it into his league; Cleomenes fled to Egypt.

wars.name: Social War (220-217 BC)
wars.outcome: 'Macedonian and Achaean victory'; the Peace of Naupactus (217) on the principle 'that every side should maintain what it currently possessed'; 'Triphylia and Phthiotis went to Macedon, while Psophis and Lasion went to Achaea'.

wars.name: First Macedonian War
wars.outcome: 'stalemate and Peace of Phoenice' (205): Rome 'would control the Parthinians, Dimallum, Bargulum, and Eugenium', Macedon kept Atintania; the Aetolians had made a separate peace in 206; Aegina was sold to Attalus.

wars.name: Philip V's Aegean and Carian campaign (Cretan War)
wars.outcome: Miletus captured and Caria invaded (201); the fleets 'clashed with Philip's off Chios and Lade' (201); the Rhodians 'appealed in 201 BC to the Roman Republic'; the Asian footholds were given up in 196.

wars.name: Second Macedonian War
wars.outcome: Roman victory: 'Macedonia gives up all possessions and client states in Orestis, Thessaly, southern Greece, Thrace and Anatolia', pays 1,000 talents and surrenders 'his whole navy except for his flagship'; 'Freedom of the Greeks' proclaimed at the Isthmian…

wars.name: Roman-Seleucid War (Macedon on the Roman side)
wars.outcome: Antiochus beaten at Thermopylae (191); the Macedonians 'occupy a number of towns in Thessaly'; Rome let Philip keep Demetrias, the Magnesian coast and parts of Athamania, Dolopia and Perrhaebia for a time.

wars.name: Third Macedonian War
wars.outcome: 'Roman victory': Pydna (22 June 168); Perseus surrendered at Samothrace; Macedon 'divided into four merides' (167); Epirus sacked ('150,000 people were enslaved'); Gentius's Illyria 'split into three cantons'.

certainty.note: Approximate frontiers throughout: the Illyrian, Dardanian and Thracian borders of Macedon, the limits of the garrison-held Greek districts, and the satrapal lines of 306-301.
